newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen rising on core PPI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen rising on core PPI.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen climbing on Thursday, aided by a mild rise in the core December producer price index, analysts said.
After initially dipping, the long bond rebounded and was up 16/32 to yield 6.80 percent.
PHIL ORLANDO, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER OF VALUE LINE'S ASSET MANAGEMENT DIVISION:

-- The core number is the number to focus on. Ex the volatile food and energy, it was only up one-tenth of one percent...It should be good for bonds...I would expect the bonds to rally, and I would expect stocks to follow.
The December Producer Price Index rose 0.5 percent compared to a 0.4 percent gain in November. The core rate, which excludes food and energy items, rose 0.1 percent.
Economists in a Reuters survey had expected a 0.3 percent rise in December PPI and a 0.1 percent rise in the core rate. ALAN ACKERMAN, MARKET STRATEGIST AT FAHNESTOCK & CO:

-- Said the 0.5 percent rise in the non-core PPI number was prompted by strength in crude oil prices, which could add to some interest rate fears in the market. "This higher number is likely to increase nervousness about higher interest rates down the road. (It) will fuel those who believe interest rates are moving higher."
